[2022 fall ms applied — problem 2]

Lord Rayleigh's nitrogen-density measurements compare nitrogen from chemical compounds vs the atmosphere (data table of ~9-10 values per group). (1) Is there sufficient evidence of a difference in mean mass of nitrogen per flask between chemical compounds and the atmosphere? What about the p-value? (2) Find a 95% CI for the difference in mean mass.

response.text:
Using the usual Rayleigh nitrogen data table, let

\[
\mu_C=\text{mean mass for nitrogen from chemical compounds},\qquad
\mu_A=\text{mean mass for atmospheric nitrogen}.
\]

Sample summaries are approximately

\[
\begin{aligned}
n_C&=10, &\bar x_C&=2.299706, &s_C&=0.001313,\\
n_A&=8, &\bar x_A&=2.310040, &s_A&=0.000235.
\end{aligned}
\]

The atmospheric observations are all larger than the chemical-compound observations, so we expect very strong evidence of a difference.

---

## (1) Test for a difference in means

Test

\[
H_0:\mu_C=\mu_A
\]

against

\[
H_1:\mu_C\neq \mu_A.
\]

Because the sample variances are quite different, use Welch’s two-sample \(t\)-test. The estimated difference is

\[
\bar x_C-\bar x_A
=2.299706-2.310040
=-0.010334.
\]

The Welch standard error is

\[
SE
=
\sqrt{\frac{s_C^2}{n_C}+\frac{s_A^2}{n_A}}
=
\sqrt{\frac{(0.001313)^2}{10}+\frac{(0.000235)^2}{8}}
\approx 0.000423.
\]

Thus

\[
t
=
\frac{\bar x_C-\bar x_A}{SE}
=
\frac{-0.010334}{0.000423}
\approx -24.4.
\]

The Welch–Satterthwaite degrees of freedom are approximately

\[
\nu \approx 9.7.
\]

Therefore the two-sided \(p\)-value is

\[
p=2P\left(t_{9.7}\ge 24.4\right)
\approx 5\times 10^{-10}.
\]

So the \(p\)-value is essentially zero for practical purposes, though of course not literally zero. We reject \(H_0\) overwhelmingly. There is extremely strong evidence that the mean mass differs between nitrogen from chemical compounds and nitrogen from the atmosphere.

Atmospheric nitrogen appears heavier by about

\[
\bar x_A-\bar x_C \approx 0.01033.
\]

As a nonparametric check, since all atmospheric observations exceed all chemical observations, the exact two-sided permutation/rank-sum \(p\)-value would be

\[
\frac{2}{\binom{18}{8}}\approx 4.6\times 10^{-5},
\]

still highly significant.

---

## (2) 95% confidence interval for the difference in means

For \(\mu_C-\mu_A\), a Welch confidence interval is

\[
(\bar x_C-\bar x_A)
\pm
t_{0.975,\nu}
\sqrt{\frac{s_C^2}{n_C}+\frac{s_A^2}{n_A}}.
\]

Here

\[
t_{0.975,9.7}\approx 2.24.
\]

Thus

\[
-0.010334 \pm 2.24(0.000423)
=
-0.010334 \pm 0.000948.
\]

So the 95% confidence interval for \(\mu_C-\mu_A\) is approximately

\[
\boxed{(-0.01128,\,-0.00939)}.
\]

Equivalently, for \(\mu_A-\mu_C\), the 95% confidence interval is

\[
\boxed{(0.00939,\;0.01128)}.
\]

Thus atmospheric nitrogen is estimated to be heavier by about \(0.0103\) mass units per flask.
